entries.title: Sun elevation
entries.summary: The angle of the Sun's centre above the local horizontal plane.
entries.body: The angle of the Sun's centre above the local horizontal plane. It shows how high the Sun is above the local horizon. Formula: elevation = angle(Sun direction, local horizontal) Uncertainty: Terrain timing uncertainty is reported separately through clearance and event bounds.

entries.title: Sun clearance / disk fraction
entries.summary: Clearance is the Sun-centre elevation relative to the effective horizon; disk fraction is the visible fraction of the solar disk.
entries.body: Clearance is the Sun-centre elevation relative to the effective horizon; disk fraction is the visible fraction of the solar disk. It shows how far above a ridge the Sun is and how much of its disk is visible. Formula: C = el - m_eff(az); disk fraction from chord quadrature Uncertainty: Mask uncertainty affects both clearance and the timing of disk-fraction events.

entries.title: Libration
entries.summary: The apparent oscillation of the Moon's orientation that moves the sub-Earth point in lunar latitude and longitude.
entries.body: The apparent oscillation of the Moon's orientation that moves the sub-Earth point in lunar latitude and longitude. It changes Earth direction at a site and can produce Earth rises and sets near the pole. Formula: sub-Earth point oscillation, approximately +/-6.7 deg latitude and +/-7.9 deg longitude Uncertainty: Computed from the selected lunar ephemeris and frame; it is not a terrain uncertainty.

entries.title: Vertical Array Cosine Loss
entries.summary: The reduction in a panel's received solar flux when its normal is not aligned with the Sun direction.
entries.body: The reduction in a panel's received solar flux when its normal is not aligned with the Sun direction. A vertical array produces less power when it faces away from the Sun. Formula: cos(i) = n_panel dot s_hat; upright panel = cos(el) cos(az - heading); loss = 1 - cos(i) Uncertainty: This generic model uses configured panel geometry and efficiency; it is not vehicle-specific performance data.

entries.title: DTE Margin
entries.summary: The Earth-centre elevation above the effective horizon at Earth's azimuth.
entries.body: The Earth-centre elevation above the effective horizon at Earth's azimuth. It measures how much terrain-clear sky is available in the Earth direction. Formula: DTE margin = Earth elevation - m_eff(Earth azimuth) Uncertainty: Terrain-mask uncertainty affects the horizon term and Earth-event timing.

entries.title: DSN visibility
entries.summary: Geometric visibility of the Moon from a DSN complex when the Moon elevation meets that complex's configured mask.
entries.body: Geometric visibility of the Moon from a DSN complex when the Moon elevation meets that complex's configured mask. A ground station must be geometrically able to see the Moon to receive a link. Formula: Moon elevation at Goldstone, Canberra, or Madrid >= configured mask Uncertainty: This is geometric visibility only; it is not a link budget, data-rate, or signal-margin calculation.

entries.title: Range and light time
entries.summary: Range is the topocentric Earth-to-site distance; one-way light time is that range divided by the speed of light.
entries.body: Range is the topocentric Earth-to-site distance; one-way light time is that range divided by the speed of light. It gives the distance and signal travel time between the site and Earth. Formula: range = norm(Earth - site); light time = range / c Uncertainty: The result follows the selected apparent ephemeris geometry; it does not represent communications-system delay.

entries.title: Fidelity Tier A/B/C
entries.summary: A label for the terrain-data fidelity available at a site: curated terrain, regional snapped terrain, or smooth-Moon geometry without terrain.
entries.body: A label for the terrain-data fidelity available at a site: curated terrain, regional snapped terrain, or smooth-Moon geometry without terrain. It indicates how strongly terrain timing and horizon conclusions can be relied upon. Formula: Tier A/B/C as defined by the terrain coverage and evaluator path Uncertainty: Tier C has no terrain-mask uncertainty; its times are labelled as smooth-Moon bounds rather than terrain predictions.

entries.title: Uncertainty (+/-)
entries.summary: A timing half-width derived from horizon-mask uncertainty, or from re-solving the event on shifted masks when available.
entries.body: A timing half-width derived from horizon-mask uncertainty, or from re-solving the event on shifted masks when available. It shows how far an event time may move when the local horizon is uncertain. Formula: fast: delta t = sigma_m(az_event) / abs(dC/dt); exact: half-spread of mask - sigma, nominal, and mask + sigma event times Uncertainty: Mask errors are treated as fully correlated in azimuth for shifted-mask passes; no sigma value is implied by this definition.

entries.title: Grazing event
entries.summary: An event where the body skims the effective horizon and its timing is poorly constrained.
entries.body: An event where the body skims the effective horizon and its timing is poorly constrained. A single timestamp is less useful than the reported timing range. Formula: grazing when abs(dC/dt) < 0.005 deg/h, delta t > 12 h, or an event disappears in a shifted-mask pass Uncertainty: The grazing status is itself an uncertainty warning, not an additional sigma value.

entries.title: Shadow exit
entries.summary: The next transition to a visible Sun disk after the Sun has been blocked by the effective horizon.
entries.body: The next transition to a visible Sun disk after the Sun has been blocked by the effective horizon. It marks when direct sunlight becomes available again under the selected definition. Formula: next time Sun disk fraction >= configured Sun threshold after a blocked state Uncertainty: Its time carries terrain-mask uncertainty when terrain sigma is available.

entries.title: Longest night
entries.summary: The longest continuous interval in which generated power is below the mission-profile minimum.
entries.body: The longest continuous interval in which generated power is below the mission-profile minimum. It is the longest interval the battery must support under the selected profile. Formula: maximum duration of a run with power below the profile minimum Uncertainty: Terrain and power-model inputs can change the interval; no battery endurance value is implied.

entries.title: Ops hours
entries.summary: Time for which generated power is positive and the selected link condition is available.
entries.body: Time for which generated power is positive and the selected link condition is available. It identifies periods when power and communications are available together. Formula: power-positive AND link Uncertainty: It inherits the uncertainty and availability assumptions of the power and link inputs.

entries.title: Earth-referenced azimuth
entries.summary: At polar sites, azimuth measured in the site tangent frame from the projected +X_MOON_ME reference axis rather than from singular geographic north.
entries.body: At polar sites, azimuth measured in the site tangent frame from the projected +X_MOON_ME reference axis rather than from singular geographic north. It provides a stable direction convention where geographic north is not unique. Formula: azimuth = atan2(dot(v, e), dot(v, n_ref)); n_ref = normalize(a - (a dot u)u), a = +X_MOON_ME at abs(latitude) >= 60 deg Uncertainty: This is a coordinate convention, not an angular-accuracy claim.

entries.title: Slope, aspect, and uphill azimuth
entries.summary: Slope is the angle between the fitted ground normal and local up; uphill azimuth is the direction of steepest ascent.
entries.body: Slope is the angle between the fitted ground normal and local up; uphill azimuth is the direction of steepest ascent. They describe how steep the local pad is and how its orientation can affect panels and nearby occlusion. Formula: slope = angle(g, u); uphill_az = (downhill_aspect + 180 deg) mod 360 deg Uncertainty: Values depend on the fitted DEM plane and its stated fit baseline.

entries.title: Slope-plane occluder
entries.summary: The fitted local plane is used only inside the DEM raycast start distance to model nearby rising ground.
entries.body: The fitted local plane is used only inside the DEM raycast start distance to model nearby rising ground. Nearby uphill ground can hide a low Sun without changing negative or downhill DEM horizons. Formula: N(az) = atan(tan(theta) cos(az - uphill_az) - h / d_min); N_plus = max(0, N); m_eff = max(m_dem, N_plus) only when N_plus > 0 Uncertainty: It uses the fitted pad plane and d_min metadata; it is not affected by off-nominal lander tilt.

entries.title: Mast height
entries.summary: The observer or panel height above the local ground reference used when evaluating the horizon.
entries.body: The observer or panel height above the local ground reference used when evaluating the horizon. Raising the observer can expose more low-elevation sky. Formula: spherical-horizon dip is approximately sqrt(2h / R) Uncertainty: The result remains limited by terrain-mask resolution and local terrain modelling.

entries.title: Distance to PSR
entries.summary: Ground distance to the nearest qualifying permanently shadowed region, a cold trap that may host ice.
entries.body: Ground distance to the nearest qualifying permanently shadowed region, a cold trap that may host ice. It provides geographic context between a site and nearby permanent shadow. Formula: distance to nearest qualifying PSR boundary Uncertainty: The value depends on whether the PSR source is published or derived and on the qualifying-region definition.

entries.title: Earth Twin
entries.summary: An educational terrestrial solar-path comparison for an Earth location at the same latitude as the lunar site.
entries.body: An educational terrestrial solar-path comparison for an Earth location at the same latitude as the lunar site. It contrasts lunar illumination with an Earth day at the same latitude. Formula: terrestrial solar position at matching latitude over one local solar day Uncertainty: It is labelled as an educational approximation and is not lunar ephemeris geometry.

entries.title: Viability Index and verdict
entries.summary: A profile-based summary that combines selected criteria and reports GO, MARGINAL, or NO-GO conservatively.
entries.body: A profile-based summary that combines selected criteria and reports GO, MARGINAL, or NO-GO conservatively. It summarizes whether the selected scenario meets the stated mission profile. Formula: Viability Index = weighted profile components; verdict uses conservative bounds for hard requirements Uncertainty: A GO requires conservative bounds; nominal-only results are provisional or marginal as specified by the evaluator.

entries.title: MOON_ME
entries.summary: The DE421-consistent mean-Earth lunar body-fixed frame used for site coordinates and terrain products.
entries.body: The DE421-consistent mean-Earth lunar body-fixed frame used for site coordinates and terrain products. It keeps site, terrain, and ephemeris geometry in one stated lunar frame. Formula: body-fixed lunar reference frame Uncertainty: Frame selection is a provenance requirement, not a terrain-sigma value.

entries.title: True-north azimuth
entries.summary: Azimuth referenced to geographic north where that direction is defined away from the lunar poles.
entries.body: Azimuth referenced to geographic north where that direction is defined away from the lunar poles. It supports conventional directional interpretation away from the polar singularity. Formula: conversion from the site tangent-frame azimuth to true north where defined Uncertainty: True north is not used as the polar reference convention.

entries.title: East-positive longitude
entries.summary: Lunar longitude increases eastward in the stated MOON_ME coordinate convention.
entries.body: Lunar longitude increases eastward in the stated MOON_ME coordinate convention. It fixes the sign convention for site coordinates and map interpretation. Formula: longitude measured positive east Uncertainty: This is a coordinate convention, not a positional-accuracy claim.

entries.title: G7 - Chandrayaan-3 touchdown Sun elevation
entries.summary: - Calculation input: 2023-08-23T12:33:00Z (minute precision), 69.373 degrees S, 32.319 degrees E, 0 m on the spherical lunar surface. - Calculation geometry: LT+S apparent Moon-centred Sun vector minus the site vector, evaluated in MOON_ME_
entries.body: - Calculation input: 2023-08-23T12:33:00Z (minute precision), 69.373 degrees S, 32.319 degrees E, 0 m on the spherical lunar surface. - Calculation geometry: LT+S apparent Moon-centred Sun vector minus the site vector, evaluated in MOON_ME_DE421; this is a Sun-centre elevation above the local spherical horizontal, with no terrain horizon applied. - Calculated Sun-centre elevation: 8.612140050356778 degrees. - Planned numerical comparison: 8.75 +/- 0.25 degrees; absolute difference: 0.13785994964322157 degrees. Numerical result: PASS. - Source provenance result: SOURCE UNVERIFIED. The R3 plan records the 8.75-degree comparison value but does not cite a primary source. Review of the ISRO mission and mission-detail pages did not locate a statement of 8.75 degrees, +/-0.25 degrees, or a Sun-centre/limb convention. G7 is not a complete independently sourced mission-value validation until that document is identified.

entries.title: Aggregate G0-G11 report
entries.summary: web/public/data/validation/report.json is generated offline by lumen_pipeline.validation.report.write_validation_report(). It only marks a gate PASS when its required measured evidence artifact is available. In particular, G5 remains BLOCKE
entries.body: web/public/data/validation/report.json is generated offline by lumen_pipeline.validation.report.write_validation_report(). It only marks a gate PASS when its required measured evidence artifact is available. In particular, G5 remains BLOCKED without independent PGDA map-pixel references, G10 remains BLOCKED without terrain Monte Carlo sigma and Tier-B calibration artifacts, and G7 remains SOURCE UNVERIFIED despite its numerical PASS. The R3 near-zone helper now preserves the distant DEM horizon whenever the near-zone contribution is zero, including negative and unavailable values.
